rows.verified: Employers must control slip and trip risks and assess those risks under workplace health and safety law.
Workplace floors should be suitable, in good condition and free from obstructions so people can move around safely.
Promptly cleaning spillages and keeping drawers closed are examples of simple controls that can prevent slips and trips.
HSE's management approach is to plan, train, organise, control, monitor and review slip-and-trip prevention.
Contamination should be prevented at source where possible, including by reviewing work activities and designing out leaks or exposed entrances.
Suitable and timely cleaning, drip trays and entrance mats can control contamination and stop it spreading.
Lighting, condensation, ice and rainwater ingress are environmental conditions that can increase slip risk and require control.
Trip prevention requires suitable clear walkways, good housekeeping, appropriate floor design and maintenance, with footwear also contributing to slip prevention.
Slip-and-trip risk depends on surface condition, contamination, task, cleaning, footwear, lighting, weather, housekeeping and the people using the area.
HSE slip-and-trip evidence is surface-, activity-, user-, maintenance-, weather- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level injury probability.
An asbestos register is a live document that must contain current information on known and presumed asbestos-containing materials and their condition.
The register should record ACM type, amount, condition, inspection dates, fibre-release potential and likelihood of disturbance.
The asbestos register should be updated at least annually or earlier when the risk from an ACM changes.
The register must include a risk assessment that helps identify and prioritise ACMs needing remedial action.
The management plan should identify responsible people, include the register and site plan, schedule condition monitoring and define information-sharing, controls and emergency procedures.
Damaged ACMs and ACMs likely to be disturbed should receive high priority in the action plan.
ACMs in good condition and unlikely to be disturbed are usually safer left in place and managed, with regular condition inspections.
Damaged ACMs must be repaired, protected, sealed or removed, and actions should be clear, time-based and reviewed when conditions or responsibilities change.
Asbestos risk depends on the building, ACM type and condition, accessibility, occupancy, maintenance and refurbishment plans, disturbance likelihood and management controls.
HSE asbestos evidence is building-, material-, condition-, activity-, control- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level exposure probability.
